body:
I think the important info is this:

> If I have the GreetingListFilter in the same module as app, everything works. It also works if the lib project is a sister module adjacent to the app.
> It does not work if the lib is a fully external artifact.
> I have added a META-INF/beans.xml in the lib for good measure, does not help.

For Hibernate ORM transformations, a `META-INF/beans.xm` is enough to find external classes from the index. Perhaps we're not using the proper index in RESTEasy Reactive?

issue.title: ParamConverter default value

body:
Another thing I noticed just now. I now added an `@jakarta.ws.rs.ext.Provider` ParamConverter for this type to the same library.
Now, I do not get the ClassNotFoundException anymore. My app works as expected.

Before that, no jax rs provider was present in the library.

The structure of the application looks weird in the sense that you have a parent `pom.xml` which has the Quarkus Maven plugin configured yet is not an applicaiton itself, but however contains a module that is an application.

I am pretty sure this kind of setup is not tested and AFAIK, it's not encouraged in any test or sample we have.

@geoand 
Thanks for looking into this.

Well yes the weird setup is caused by the reproducer. I just wanted to create something that fails, and that was the first thing I tested which did indeed fail :).

My real world application fails with the same exception.
In that one the lib is completly seperate from the quarkus application.

The quarkus application itself is multi module project.
Quarkus plugin is defined in pluginmanagement of parent.
And as plugin itself in the module which should be launched during quarkus:dev.
The same setup as any of my other apps running in production.

So yes, please look deeper into this. Just cause there is a stumbling block does not mean the rest of the reproducer is invalid :)

(sorry if this comes of as harsh - I just hate situations like this. one mistake done and everything invalid? thats stupid)

I understand your point, no offense taken.

Let me try and explain my point of view a little better: I have to look at a bunch of issue day in and day out in addition to doing new development. 
Lots of eople such as yourself do an amazing job of making my job a lot easier by eliminating the guesswork and allowing me to spend very little time on setting up an environment where the problem manifests.
But when something like this happens, it's not an optimal use of my time to try and guess what the real world application looks like and try to recreate it. 
Additionally, it's not uncommon for people to find issues in their own setups when they try to provide a proper reproducer.

So  if you don't mind, can you please update the reproduce with a more typical Maven multi-module and dig in deeper to try and figure out what's going on.

Thanks
